families.description: Performs a comparison between two parameters in a command.

entries.name: c:<
entries.description: Less than. In DE, the first DE ID is for < and the second DE ID is for c:<.

entries.name: c:<=
entries.description: Less than or equal. In DE, the first DE ID is for <= and the second DE ID is for c:<=.

entries.name: c:>
entries.description: Greater than. In DE, the first DE ID is for > and the second DE ID is for c:>.

entries.name: c:>=
entries.description: Greater than or equal. In DE, the first DE ID is for >= and the second DE ID is for c:>=.

entries.name: c:==
entries.description: Equal. Note: one equals sign (=) is an assignment operator used in the mathOp operator. Always use "==" when you want to compare. In DE, the first DE ID is for == and the second DE ID is for c:==.

entries.name: c:!=
entries.description: Not equal. In DE, the first DE ID is for != and the second DE ID is for c:!=.

entries.name: g:<
entries.description: Less than the goal's value.

entries.name: g:<=
entries.description: Less than or equal to the goal's value.

entries.name: g:>
entries.description: Greater than the goal's value.

entries.name: g:>=
entries.description: Greater than or equal to the goal's value.

entries.name: g:==
entries.description: Equal to the goal's value. Note: one equals sign (=) is an assignment operator used in the mathOp operator. Always use "==" when you want to compare.

entries.name: g:!=
entries.description: Not equal to the goal's value.

entries.name: s:<
entries.description: Less than the strategic number's value.

entries.name: s:<=
entries.description: Less than or equal to the strategic number's value.

entries.name: s:>
entries.description: Greater than the strategic number's value.

entries.name: s:>=
entries.description: Greater than or equal to the strategic number's value.

entries.name: s:==
entries.description: Equal to the strategic number's value. Note: one equals sign (=) is an assignment operator used in the mathOp operator. Always use "==" when you want to compare.

entries.name: s:!=
entries.description: Not equal to the strategic number's value.

families.description: Performs a comparison between two parameters in a command.

entries.name: c:
entries.description: Treats the second compared parameter in the command as a constant when doing the comparison. If the second parameter to be compared is a defined value, such as a goal or a unit type, this will use the numeric Id value assigned to this parameter. Note: this prefix is optional for compareOp operators. You can also use the comparison operators without the prefix.

entries.name: g:
entries.description: Treats the second compared parameter in the command as a GoalId and compare to the value stored in that goal. This prefix is required when comparing to a goal's value.

entries.name: s:
entries.description: Treats the second compared parameter in the command as a Strategic Number and compare to the value set by that strategic number. This prefix is required when comparing to the strategic number's value.

families.description: Performs a math operation between two parameters in the command.

entries.name: c:=
entries.description: Set the first operand equal to the constant value of the second operand.

entries.name: c:+
entries.description: Add the constant value of the second operand to the first operand.

entries.name: c:-
entries.description: Subtract the constant value of the second operand from the first operand.

entries.name: c:*
entries.description: Multiply the first operand by the constant value of the second operand.

entries.name: c:z/
entries.description: Divide the first operand by the constant value of the second operand. The quotient is truncated (rounded down) to the nearest integer.

entries.name: c:/
entries.description: Divide the first operand by the constant value of the second operand. The quotient is rounded to the nearest integer.

entries.name: c:mod
entries.description: Divide the first operand by the constant value of the second operand. Store the remainder instead of the quotient.

entries.name: c:min
entries.description: Store the smallest value between the first operand and the constant value of the second operand.

entries.name: c:max
entries.description: Store the largest value between the first operand and the constant value of the second operand.

entries.name: c:neg
entries.description: Negate the constant value of the second operand and store the result in the first operand. If the constant is already negative, this will store its positive value.

entries.name: c:%/
entries.description: Divide the first operand by the constant value of the second operand, and convert the quotient to a percent, truncated (not rounded) to the nearest integer, i.e. (first operand / second operand * 100).

entries.name: c:%*
entries.description: Treat the constant value of the second operand as a percentage and find that percentage of the first parameter, truncated (not rounded) to the nearest integer, i.e. (first operand * second operand / 100).

families.description: Controls the attack stance of military units.

entries.description: Do not set a new attack stance.

entries.name: stance-aggressive
entries.description: Aggressive Stance. Soldiers will attack all enemy objects in line of sight and chase them.

entries.name: stance-defensive
entries.description: Defensive Stance. Soldiers will attack most enemy objects in line of sight, but they will return to their original location if the enemy objects leave the area.

entries.name: stance-stand-ground
entries.description: Stand Ground Stance. Soldiers will only attack enemy objects if they can attack the unit from their current location.

entries.name: stance-no-attack
entries.description: No Attack Stance. Soldiers will only attack if ordered to target an object through DUC.

families.description: The id of an attribute to modify, such as attribute-hp.

entries.name: attribute-hp
entries.description: The object's hit points.

entries.name: attribute-los
entries.description: The object's line of sight.

entries.name: attribute-obj-max
entries.description: Unknown.

entries.name: attribute-radius-x
entries.description: Unknown. Possibly the radius of the object's size in the x direction.

entries.name: attribute-radius-y
entries.description: Unknown. Possibly the radius of the object's size in the y direction.

entries.name: attribute-speed
entries.description: The object's speed. Probably multiplied by 100, but this is untested.

entries.name: attribute-turn-speed
entries.description: The time it takes the object to turn from one rotation/facing direction to the next. Most objects' turn speed is zero, but this is observable for ships and trebuchets.

entries.name: attribute-armor
entries.description: The object's armor. Unknown whether this is melee armor, pierce armor, or both, but it's likely just melee armor. It seems like there isn't a way to choose which armor type to modify, or there is a complex formula that allows you to specify the armor type and amount in a single value.

entries.name: attribute-weapon
entries.description: Unknown. Probably the object's attack. It's possible there is a complex formula that allows you to specify the type of attack/attack bonus and the amount in a single value.

entries.name: attribute-speed-of-attack
entries.description: The object's attack speed. Unknown whether this is given in seconds or milliseconds, but probably the latter.

entries.name: attribute-hit-chance
entries.description: Unknown. Probably the object's accuracy. Likely multiplied by 100.

entries.name: attribute-weapon-range
entries.description: The object's range.

entries.name: attribute-work-rate
entries.description: The object's work rate. This attribute is primarily relevant for buildings, which determines the speed that units and techs are trained and researched.

entries.name: attribute-carry-capacity
entries.description: The amount the object can carry. This affects the resource capacity villagers can carry and also the amount of resources that Gaia/player owned resources can hold.

entries.name: attribute-base-armor
entries.description: Similar to attribute-armor. Untested, but this likely affects the original armor amount, so it wouldn't display as + or - like it would for blacksmith armor upgrades.

entries.name: attribute-missile-id
entries.description: The ID of the object's projectile. See the Proj. ID in the Objects Table to get the projectile IDs of each unit.

entries.name: attribute-building-facet
entries.description: Unknown. Likely the rotation the building faces, though most buildings only have one direction anyway.

entries.name: attribute-defensive-terrain
entries.description: Unknown. Could be the same as Terrain Defense Bonus from Advanced Genie Editor.

entries.name: attribute-targetting-type
entries.description: Unknown.

entries.name: attribute-minimum-weapon-range
entries.description: The object's minimum range.

entries.name: attribute-attribute-amount-held
entries.description: Unknown. The attribute-attribute in the attribute name isn't a typo. ;)

entries.name: attribute-area-effect
entries.description: Likely the object's blast radius.

entries.name: attribute-search-radius
entries.description: The object's search radius. This is often equal to LOS, and it determines the radius where the object will respond to enemy units.

entries.name: attribute-hidden-damage-resist
entries.description: Unknown. Could be the same as the Bonus Damage Resist field from Advanced Genie Editor.

entries.name: attribute-icon-id
entries.description: The ID of the object's icon.

entries.name: attribute-fire-missile-at-frame
entries.description: Likely the frame delay, the number of graphical frames to must be displayed from the attack animation before the projectile will fire.

entries.name: attribute-area-effect-level.
entries.description: Likely the object's blast attack level. The blast damage for objects with level 3 or higher only damage the targeted object. The blast damage for objects with level 2 will damage nearby objects that are within the blast radius of the attack. The blast damage for objects with level 1 can damage trees. The blast damage for objects with level 0 can damage all resources. Note: many buildings and cavalry units have blast level 0, so it is wise to check if the blast radius is > 0 before checking the blast level.

entries.name: attribute-blast-defense-level
entries.description: The object's blast defense level. The object will receive blast damage from units with a blast attack level greater than or equal to the object's blast defense level.

entries.name: attribute-shown-attack
entries.description: The object's shown attack. A + or - value will be displayed in the interface if the actual attack is higher or lower than the shown attack, respectively.

entries.name: attribute-shown-range
entries.description: The object's shown range. A + or - value will be displayed in the interface if the actual range is higher or lower than the shown attack, respectively.

entries.name: attribute-shown-melee-armor
entries.description: The object's shown melee armor. A + or - value will be displayed in the interface if the actual melee armor is higher or lower than the shown attack, respectively. Uncertain if shown pierce armor can be affected with this attribute.

entries.name: attribute-name-id
entries.description: Likely the language ID location of the object's name.

entries.name: attribute-description-id
entries.description: Likely the language ID location of the object's description.

entries.name: attribute-terrain-restriction
entries.description: The terrain the object can travel or be placed on. Likely the same as the Terrain Table field in Advanced Genie Editor.

entries.name: attribute-death-spawn-obj
entries.description: The ID of a new object that is spawned when an object dies. This is usually the unit's corpse or ruins, but it is used by the Konnik to spawn a dismounted Konnik when the mounted Konnik dies.

entries.name: attribute-hotkey-id
entries.description: Likely the language ID location of the letter for the object's default hotkey.

entries.name: attribute-resource-cost
entries.description: Likely let's you change the ResourceType cost for a resource besides food, wood, gold, or stone.

entries.name: attribute-creation-time
entries.description: The amount of time to create the object, in seconds.

entries.name: attribute-garrison-arrows
entries.description: Likely either the extra number of projectiles the object will fire or the max number of arrows the object can fire when fully garrisoned. Not sure how this differs from attribute-max-dup-missiles.

entries.name: attribute-food-cost
entries.description: The object's food cost.

entries.name: attribute-wood-cost
entries.description: The object's wood cost.

entries.name: attribute-gold-cost
entries.description: The object's gold cost.

entries.name: attribute-stone-cost
entries.description: The object's stone cost.

entries.name: attribute-max-dup-missiles
entries.description: Likely either the extra number of projectiles the object will fire or the max number of arrows the object can fire when fully garrisoned. Not sure how this differs from attribute-garrison-arrows

entries.name: attribute-garrison-heal-rate
entries.description: The object's heal rate for units that are garrisoned inside. Likely multiplied by 100 or 1000 (not sure which, sorry).

entries.name: attribute-regenration-rate
entries.description: Note the [incorrect] spelling. The speed the object will heal at. Likely multiplied by 100 or 1000 (not sure which, sorry).

entries.name: ability-to-maintain-distance
entries.description: Chance that a computer player's ranged unit will maintain the distance. Range is 0-100, and the values are opposite from what you'd expect! When set to 0, ranged units will frequently move back to maintain distance. When set to 100, ranged units will not move back. However, this behavior only works on units are not following a move, patrol, or attack move command and are simply using their automatic attacking behavior. Setting snEnablePatrolAttack may also disable this behavior.

entries.name: ability-to-dodge-missiles
entries.description: Chance of a computer player's unit dodging a missile. Range is 0-100, and the values are opposite from what you'd expect! When set to 0, units will try to dodge immediately upon seeing a projectile in the air. When set to 100, they have to hit first to react. Projectiles from siege-weapon-class and unpacked-trebuchet-class (913 and 954, not including scorpions) are always dodged, no matter what this parameter is set to. Note that while setting this to 0 might seem obvious, it may prove better to experiment especially depending on what enemy units you are facing and what units you are producing. For example, navy units have turn rates and so can suffer.

families.description: The action to perform with the selected units.

entries.name: action-default
entries.description: Equivalent of a right-click for all objects in the local list on the point or target object(s). For up-target-point this is the same as action-move.

entries.name: action-move
entries.description: Units in the local list will move to the point or the location of the target object(s).

entries.name: action-patrol
entries.description: Units in the local list will patrol to the point or the location of the target object(s).

entries.name: action-guard
entries.description: Units in the local list will guard the target object(s). For up-target-point this is the same as action-move.

entries.name: action-follow
entries.description: Units in the local list will follow the target object(s). For up-target-point this is the same as action-move.

entries.name: action-stop
entries.description: Objects in the local list will stop their current action.

entries.name: action-ground
entries.description: Units in the local list will attack ground at the point or against the target object(s).

entries.name: action-garrison
entries.description: Units in the local list will garrison inside the target object(s). For up-target-point this is the same as action-move.

entries.name: action-delete
entries.description: Deletable objects in the local list will be deleted.

entries.name: action-unload
entries.description: Buildings in the local list will ungarrison to the target point. Siege (class 913) in the local list will eject in place. Transport ships in the local list will unload at the target point. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-train
entries.description: Buildings in the local list will train units. To train units, use this syntax: (up-target-point EscrowGoalId action-train typeOp TypeId). Example: (up-target-point 0 action-train c: spearman-line). For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-gather
entries.description: Buildings in the local list will set their gather point at the target point or at the location of the target object(s).

entries.name: action-lock
entries.description: Gates in the local list will toggle their locked state. If they are locked, they will unlock. If they are unlocked, they will lock. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-work
entries.description: Buildings in the local list will send garrisoned villagers back to work. Same as clicking the Send Back to Work button. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-ungarrison
entries.description: Units in the local list will be ungarrisoned from the building they are garrisoned inside. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-drop-relic
entries.description: Monastery units in the local list will drop any relics they are carrying. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-pack
entries.description: Trebuchets in the local list will pack. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-unpack
entries.description: Trebuchets in the local list will unpack. For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

entries.name: action-none
entries.description: The current actions of the objects in the local list will not change.

entries.name: action-attack-move
entries.description: Must be defined with a defconst. Only available in DE. Units in the local list will attack move to the point or the location of the target object(s).

entries.name: action-transform
entries.description: Must be defined with a defconst. Only available in DE. Rathas in the local list will switch between melee and ranged mode.

entries.name: action-research
entries.description: Must be defined with a defconst. Only available in DE. Researches a tech at a building in the local list. Use this syntax: (up-target-point EscrowGoalId action-research typeOp TypeId). Example: (up-target-point 0 action-research c: ri-loom). For up-target-objects this is the same as action-none.

families.description: Check specific information about the selected target object.

entries.name: object-data-index
entries.description: Use only with up-remove-objects. This will remove objects by the search index. Returns -2 for up-get-object-data and up-object-data.

entries.name: object-data-id
entries.description: The object's map ID. All objects on the map will have a different map object ID in the order that the object appeared on the map. Same as the Id parameter.

entries.name: object-data-type
entries.description: The object's type, just like unit-type-count. Note: this always returns the object-data-base-type for a unit/building line in non-scenario games. For example, if the object is a man-at-arms, this will return 74 (militiaman). If you want to get the current upgraded unit type, use object-data-upgrade-type instead. In summary, this ObjectData functions just like object-data-base-type, except in scenarios where upgraded versions of units can be placed on the map from the start of the game.

entries.name: object-data-class
entries.description: The object's class. See ClassId for a description and list of object classes.

entries.name: object-data-category
entries.description: The object's category. Use Advanced Genie Editor to determine an object's category (called "Type"). Category 10 = Eye Candy and resources. Category 20 = Animated map objects. Category 30 = Dead units and fish. Category 60 = Projectiles. Category 70 = Units. Category 80 = Buildings.

entries.name: object-data-cmdid
entries.description: The object's command ID. See CmdId for a description and list of object command IDs.

entries.name: object-data-action
entries.description: The object's action. See ActionId for a description and list of object action IDs. This data is NOT available for units marching in formation. When the objects is idle or marching in formation, this data returns -1.

entries.name: object-data-order
entries.description: The object's order. See OrderId for a description and list of object order IDs. This data is NOT available for units marching in formation. When the object is not executing an order or marching in formation, this data returns -1.

entries.name: object-data-target
entries.description: The object-data-class of the object that the object is targeting. This data is NOT available for units marching in formation. In UP, when the object is not targeting anything or is marching in formation toward the target, this data returns -1. In DE, when the object is not targeting anything or is marching in formation toward the target, this data returns -2.

entries.name: object-data-point-x
entries.description: The x-coordinate of the tile the object is on.

entries.name: object-data-point-y
entries.description: The y-coordinate of the tile the object is on.

entries.name: object-data-hitpoints
entries.description: The object's current hit points. This takes into account any damage the object has suffered.

entries.name: object-data-maxhp
entries.description: The object's maximum possible hit points. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-range
entries.description: The object's range. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-speed
entries.description: The object's speed, multiplied by 100. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses. In UP, deer and wolves return their walking speed, even when running. In DE, deer and wolves return different speeds depending on whether they are walking or running.

entries.name: object-data-dropsite
entries.description: The UnitId of the dropsite that belongs to the resource that is being gathered by the object. This will always be the UnitId of a mill, lumber camp, and mining camp for food, wood, and gold/stone, even if resources are being dropped off at a town center. A villager who hasn't been assigned a role (name change) will also given the result "mill". All villagers given a non-gathering task and all other objects will return -1.

entries.name: object-data-resource
entries.description: The object's Resource type. If the object isn't a resource, object-data-resource is -1.

entries.name: object-data-carry
entries.description: The amount of resources an object is carrying. This includes the amount of resources a villager is holding, the amount of food left in decaying animals, monk faith generation, flares, and unit corpses. It does not include resources that trade carts and trade cogs are carrying. Flares and corpses have carry because of a decay timer that controls when they are removed from the map. Objects that cannot carry resources return 0.

entries.name: object-data-garrisoned
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is garrisoned. Otherwise, 0.

entries.name: object-data-garrison-count
entries.description: The number of units garrisoned inside the object.

entries.name: object-data-status
entries.description: The status of the object. See ObjectStatus for a list of possible object states.

entries.name: object-data-player
entries.description: The player number that the object belongs to, between 0 and 8.

entries.name: object-data-attack-stance
entries.description: The attack stance of the object. See AttackStance for a list of attack stances. Objects that cannot change their attack stance appear to have an attack stance of 0, the same as stance-aggressive.

entries.name: object-data-action-time
entries.description: The game time in milliseconds when the object's most recently moved. In UP, it was reported that attacking an object could reset this to 0, so it's possible that this object data works differently in UP.

entries.name: object-data-target-id
entries.description: The ID of the object that the object is targeting. This data is NOT available for units marching in formation. When an object is not targeting anything or is marching in formation, this data returns -1.

entries.name: object-data-formation-id
entries.description: The formation of the object. Unfortunately, this object data doesn't match Formation and it seems to be able to change depending on the object's action, even if the formation type isn't changed. When not marching in formation, this returns -1.

entries.name: object-data-patrolling
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is patrolling, otherwise 0. This data is not affected by snEnablePatrolAttack.

entries.name: object-data-strike-armor
entries.description: The object's current strike (melee) armor, including researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-pierce-armor
entries.description: The object's current pierce armor, including researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-base-attack
entries.description: The object's current base attack, including researched technologies and civ bonuses. Attack bonus amounts are not included and cannot be detected by AIs. :(

entries.name: object-data-locked
entries.description: Returns 1 if the gate object (gate or palisade gate) is locked, otherwise 0. Non-gate objects return -2.

entries.name: object-data-garrison-id
entries.description: Unknown. Doesn't seem to be the map-based Id of the building or unit the object is garrisoned inside. If the object is not garrisoned, object-data-garrison-id is -2.

entries.name: object-data-train-count
entries.description: The number of units are queued at the object for training, including the unit currently being trained. Objects that cannot train units return -2.

entries.name: object-data-tasks-count
entries.description: The number of units that are tasked to work on the object (sometimes 2+ per command, for example a lumberjack assigned to a tree may show 2 when the lumberjack is walking with a gather command/hunt command).

entries.name: object-data-attacker-count
entries.description: The number of objects that are attacking the object. Ranged units are only counted when a projectile is actively flying through the air toward the unit. Melee units are only counted after they have caused damage and will continue to be counted as attackers until they are retasked or switch to a different target. This is not increased for certain situations, like hunting.

entries.name: object-data-attacker-id
entries.description: The map-based Id of the enemy unit or building that is attacking the object. If multiple objects are attacking, it's either the object that most recently attacked or the attacker with the lowest map-based ID. When attacked by ranged units, the ID is set when the projectile is launched, but when attacked by melee units the ID is not set until the melee unit causes damage. Not set for certain situations, like hunting. Doesn't work with villagers. If the object is not under attack, this returns -2. Once the ID is set, there appears to be about a 30 second cooldown until the ID is reset back to -2 if no other unit has attacked in that 30 second window.

entries.name: object-data-under-attack
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is being attacked, otherwise 0. When attacked by ranged units, this data returns 1 only after the projectile is launched, but when attacked by melee units this data returns 1 only after the melee unit causes damage. It remains at 1 until the attacking unit switches its task or target. Not set for certain situations, like hunting. Doesn't work for villagers. Once set to 1, there appears to be about a 30 second cooldown until the data is reset back to 0 if no other unit has attacked in that 30 second window.

entries.name: object-data-attack-timer
entries.description: Likely a timer countdown for building objects. When a building is attacked, a 60-second timer starts and counts down toward 0. This timer is reset every time the building is attacked. Non-building objects always return 0.

entries.name: object-data-point-z
entries.description: Likely get's the object's z-location. Only objects flying in the air like projectiles and birds have a z-coordinate > 0.

entries.name: object-data-precise-x
entries.description: The object's precise x-location, multiplied by 100. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile.

entries.name: object-data-precise-y
entries.description: The object's precise y-location, multiplied by 100. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile.

entries.name: object-data-precise-z
entries.description: The object's precise z-location, multiplied by 100. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile. Only objects flying in the air like projectiles and birds have a z-coordinate > 0.

entries.name: object-data-researching
entries.description: Returns 1 when the object is researching a technology, otherwise 0. Objects that cannot research technologies return -2.

entries.name: object-data-tile-position
entries.description: The object's position on the tile. See snTargetPointAdjustment for details on the tile positions.

entries.name: object-data-tile-inverse
entries.description: The opposite tile position of the object's position on the tile. If the object is on the top part of the tile (position 2), object-data-tile-inverse will be 4 (bottom). See snTargetPointAdjustment for details on the tile positions.

entries.name: object-data-distance
entries.description: The object's distance from the target-point. This does not take obstacles into account. It is simply a distance formula calculation between the target point's location and the object's location. Do not use object-data-distance with a precise target point. Instead, use object-data-to-precise to calculate the precise distance to a precise target point.

entries.name: object-data-precise-distance
entries.description: The object's precise distance from the target-point, x 100. This does not take obstacles into account. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile. It is simply a distance formula calculation between the target point's location and the object's location, multiplied by 100. It assumes the target point is a normal point, so do not use object-data-precise-distance with a precise target point. Instead, use object-data-to-precise to calculate the precise distance to a precise target point.

entries.name: object-data-full-distance
entries.description: The object's precise distance from the target-point, squared. For example, if the precise distance is 41.34 tiles, object-data-full-distance will be 1709.

entries.name: object-data-map-zone-id
entries.description: The map zone that the object is on. Each landmass is assigned a different zone ID, so this is useful to determine if objects are on different islands.

entries.name: object-data-on-mainland
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is on the same landmass as the starting landmass, otherwise 0.

entries.name: object-data-idling
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is idle, otherwise 0. Does not work with villagers.

entries.name: object-data-move-x
entries.description: The x-coordinate of the object's most recent targeted location. Applies to move, attack, and other related commands. Automatic activities such as chasing enemy units will not set a new location because a direct command was never issued. If the object has never targeted a location, this will return -1.

entries.name: object-data-move-y
entries.description: The y-coordinate of the object's most recent targeted location. Applies to move, attack, and other related commands. Automatic activities such as chasing enemy units will not set a new location because a direct command was never issued. If the object has never targeted a location, this will return -1.

entries.name: object-data-precise-move-x
entries.description: The precise x-coordinate of the object's most recent targeted location, multiplied by 100. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile. Applies to move, attack, and other related commands. Automatic activities such as chasing enemy units will not set a new location because a direct command was never issued. If the object has never targeted a location, this will return -100.

entries.name: object-data-precise-move-y
entries.description: The precise y-coordinate of the object's most recent targeted location, multiplied by 100. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile. Applies to move, attack, and other related commands. Automatic activities such as chasing enemy units will not set a new location because a direct command was never issued. If the object has never targeted a location, this will return -100.

entries.name: object-data-reload-time
entries.description: The object's reload time, in milliseconds. This is the time between subsequent attacks. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses. For the time remaining until the unit can attack again, use object-data-next-attack.

entries.name: object-data-next-attack
entries.description: The time until the object can attack again, in milliseconds. The time is a countdown that starts at the object's object-data-reload-time and counts down to 0. The countdown begins at the start of the unit's attack animation. One important thing to note is that damage is not dealt at the start of a unit's attack animation, but instead they have an attack delay. You can find the attack delays of each object with object-data-attack-delay. For example, a crossbowman's reload time without Thumb Ring is 2000 milliseconds, and their attack delay is 350 milliseconds. So, if the object-data-next-attack is below 1650 (2000 minus 350), that means that the crossbowman has shot their arrow and is waiting until they can shoot again.

entries.name: object-data-train-site
entries.description: The BuildingId that can train the object.

entries.name: object-data-train-time
entries.description: The time it takes to train the object, assuming the object's train site has a "work rate" of 1.0. This does not take into account technologies like Conscription or civ bonuses which train units faster by increasing the building's work rate rather than modifying the train time of individual units.

entries.name: object-data-blast-radius
entries.description: The object's blast radius, multiplied by 100. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-blast-level
entries.description: The type of blast radius the object has. The blast damage for objects with level 3 or higher only damage the targeted object. The blast damage for objects with level 2 will damage nearby objects that are within the blast radius of the attack. The blast damage for objects with level 1 can damage trees. The blast damage for objects with level 0 can damage all resources. Note: many buildings and cavalry units have blast level 0, so it is wise to check if the blast radius is > 0 before checking the blast level.

entries.name: object-data-progress-type
entries.description: The type of progress the object has (training or researching). Objects that cannot train or research return -2. An object that can train or research but is doing neither will return 0. If the object is training or researching, a value from the pProgressType list will be returned: progress-type-train (a value of 102) or progress-type-research (a value of 103).

entries.name: object-data-progress-value
entries.description: The percent completion for the unit the object is training or the technology the object is researching. Objects that cannot train or research return -2.

entries.name: object-data-min-range
entries.description: The minium range of the object. This includes researched technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: object-data-target-time
entries.description: The amount of time, in milliseconds, that the object has been attacking its current target. Also seems to return negative amounts when a villager is herding animals for some reason. Objects that aren't attacking return -2.

entries.name: object-data-heresy
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is benefitting from Heresy, otherwise 0.

entries.name: object-data-gather-type
entries.description: The Resource that the villager is gathering, or -1 if the object isn't gathering a resource. Trade units return 3 when they are carrying gold back to the Market or Dock. Monasteries don't return 3 when relics are garrisoned inside. In DE, object-data-gather-type won't change while villagers are carrying resources of a different type. Using snKeystates set to 2, we can force them to drop their resources when they are reassigned and this causes object-data-gather-type to change immediately. Note that it will change immediately either way when villagers are not carrying resources of a different type. It also still "correctly" reset to -1 when the villager is returning from the camp after dropping off their resources. WARNING: when villagers drop resources they may instantly be reassigned by the game engine if the gatherer percentages are not met.

entries.name: object-data-language-id
entries.description: The pLanguageId of the object's current name. This is one way to determine the task a villager has been given.

entries.name: object-data-group-flag
entries.description: The group number that the object has been assigned with up-modify-group-flag. If the object hasn't been assigned to a group, object-data-group-flag returns -2.

entries.name: object-data-hero-flags
entries.description: The sum of hero flags set on the unit. Most of these, except for Flag 1 are set through UP effects in scenarios or random map scripts. Standard heroes return 1. Flag 1 = full hero. Flag 2 = disabled conversions. Flag 4 = enable hero heal rate. Flag 8 = set defensive attack stance as default. Flag 16 = force the unit to use a Protective Formation (maybe puts the hero in center of box formation?). Flag 32 = enables suicide attacks. Flag 64 = enable blast radius. Flag 128 = disable attack ground. Flag 256 = clear all flags.

entries.name: object-data-hero
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is a hero (has hero flag 1 set, see object-data-hero-flags for details), otherwise 0.

entries.name: object-data-auto-heal
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is a full hero (hero flag 1) or it has the auto-heal hero flag set (hero flag 4, see object-data-hero-flags for details). Berserks return 0 because their health regeneration is coded separately from hero health regeneration.

entries.name: object-data-no-convert
entries.description: Returns 1 if the object is a full hero (hero flag 1) or it has the no-convert flag set (hero flag 2, see object-data-hero-flags for details). Unconvertible buildings like town centers and castles return 0 because their no-convert feature is hard-coded separately from hero non-conversion.

entries.name: object-data-frame-delay
entries.description: The object's frame delay. Frame delay is the number of graphics frames between the start of the attack animation and the launch of the projectile. Unfortunately, the duration of each frame in the animation is different for each unit, so it's very difficult to calculate the precise duration of frame delay. Use object-data-attack-delay to determine the unit's attack delay.

entries.name: object-data-attack-count
entries.description: The number of times the object has tried to damage its most recent target. This number is not reset to 0 until a new target has been found. If the object has never targeted anything, this returns 0.

entries.name: object-data-to-precise
entries.description: The precise distance from the object to the target point, x 100, assuming the target point is a precise point. This does not take obstacles into account. Precise locations are accurate to 1/100 of a tile. It is simply a distance formula calculation between the target point's location and the object's location, multiplied by 100. However, it assumes the target point is a precise point, so it divides the target point's location by 100 before calculating the distance, even if the target point was set with up-set-target-point instead of up-set-precise-target-point. If the target point is a normal point, not a precise point, use object-data-precise-distance to calculate the precise distance between an object and a normal target point.

entries.name: object-data-base-type
entries.description: The ObjectId of the first unit/building in the object's line. For example, this returns 74 (militiaman) when the object is a Long Swordsman.

entries.name: object-data-upgrade-type
entries.description: The true ObjectId of the object. If the object is a man-at-arms, this will return 75 (man-at-arms). This ObjectData was needed because object-data-type functions just like object-data-base-type under in non-scenario games.

entries.name: object-data-ownership*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-ownership 83). Returns the player number that owns the object or is the most dominant player nearby. Returns -2 if the object cannot be captured. Returns -1 if it can be captured but no player units are nearby. Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-capture-flag*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-capture-flag 84). The capture type of an object owned by gaia or another player. 0 = capture never, 1 = capture once, 2 = capture multiple times, 3 = capture livestock/artifact. Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-charge-attack-type*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-charge-attack-type 85). Gets the charge attack type. Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-charge-attack-max*
entries.description: DE only. Gets the maximum charge attack value (x100). Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-charge-attack-amount*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-charge-attack-amount 87). Gets the selected object current charge attack amount (x100). Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-charge-attack-regeneration-rate*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-charge-attack-regeneration-rate 88). Gets the regeneration rate of a charge attack (x100). Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-charge-attack-event-type*
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst before use with (defconst object-data-charge-attack-event-type 89). Gets the charge attack event type. Returns -2 on UP or WK.

entries.name: object-data-attack-delay*
entries.description: DE only. The object's attack delay in milliseconds. Damage is not dealt at the start of a unit's attack animation, but instead they have an attack delay. For ranged units, the attack delay is equal to: (object-data-frame-delay / Number Attack Animation Frames) * Attack Animation Duration. For melee units, the attack delay is equal to: Attack Animation Duration / 2. For example, a crossbowman's reload time without Thumb Ring is 2000 milliseconds, and the time length of their projectile delay is 0.35 seconds, or 350 milliseconds. So, if the object-data-next-attack is below 1650 (2000 minus 350), that means that the crossbowman has shot their arrow and is waiting until they can shoot again.

entries.description: Same placement as build-forward, except that locations are affected by snPlacementZoneSize. Setting large values for sn-placement-zone-size can surround the enemy player with the forward building.

entries.name: place-control
entries.description: Allows more controlled building placement. Uses the settings from up-set-placement-data, snPlacementZoneSize, snPlacementFailDelta, and snPlacementToCenter to control building placement. See this image for an explanation: http://i.imgur.com/FUpDF.gif

entries.name: place-point
entries.description: Allows placement for a building at the point specified by up-set-target-point. Building placement with place-point is affected by snPlacementZoneSize, but it is not affected by up-set-placement-data, snPlacementFailDelta, or snPlacementToCenter.

families.description: The position type, a predefined position that can be stored in a point.

entries.name: position-center
entries.description: The center of the map.

entries.name: position-opposite
entries.description: The point on the opposite side of the map from position-self. It is found reflecting position-self across the center of the map. Returns the point (-1,-1) when all TCs are destroyed.

entries.name: position-corner
entries.description: The location of the corner closest to position-self. Returns the point (-1,-1) when all TCs are destroyed.

entries.name: position-enemy
entries.description: A random location +/- 8 tiles from the target player's nearest non-wall building. If the enemy hasn't been found, this is the same as position-opposite.

entries.name: position-border
entries.description: The point on a border that is closest to position-self. Returns the point (-1,-1) when all TCs are destroyed.

entries.name: position-mirror
entries.description: The expected position of the mirrored opponent on the opposite team, found by mirroring from position-self across the line that separates teams. Returns the point (-1,-1) when all TCs are destroyed.

entries.name: position-flank
entries.description: The expected position where the nearest enemy flank player should be, found by evaluating all of the scout-opposite points for all members of the team and picking the closest point. Returns the point (-1,-1) when all TCs are destroyed.

entries.name: position-zero
entries.description: The leftmost point on the map, where x and y are 0.

entries.name: position-map-size
entries.description: The rightmost point on the map, where x and y equal the map size.

entries.name: position-self
entries.description: The location of the player's oldest Town Center. When all TCs are destroyed, position-self is the location of the most-recently destroyed TC.

entries.name: position-target
entries.description: The location of the nearest non-wall building of the target player. Not defined if the target player is the same as my-player-number.

entries.name: position-focus
entries.description: The location of the nearest non-wall building of the focus player. Not defined if the focus player is the same as my-player-number.

entries.name: position-object
entries.description: The location of the target object.

entries.name: position-point
entries.description: The location of the target point.

entries.description: DE only. The research has been manually disabled, probably through a scenario trigger. If a tech is unavailable in a civ's tech tree, the status will be research-unavailable.

entries.name: research-unavailable
entries.description: The research is not available, either because the age or technology prerequisites haven't been met, the research is not available in the civ's tech tree, or building requirements haven't been met (for age techs only).

entries.name: research-available
entries.description: The age, technology, building (for age techs), and civilization requirements for the research have been met, but the player hasn't started researching the research yet. Techs can still be considered research-available even if the AI doesn't have a building that can research them.

entries.name: research-pending
entries.description: The research is currently being researched. Doesn't count queued techs.

entries.name: research-complete

entries.name: research-queued

entries.name: amount-research-summation
entries.description: Likely a technology's total cost. Could be used to calculate part of the player's economic score.

entries.name: amount-relic-income-summation
entries.description: The total relic gold generated for the player. Likely is equal to Relic Gold amount in the achievements screen. Untested whether this includes feitoria gold income.

entries.name: amount-trade-income-summation
entries.description: The total gold generated from trade units for the player. Likely is equal to Trade Profit in the achievements screen.

entries.name: amount-castle
entries.description: Likely the number of player's castles currently standing. Probably isn't equal to Total Castles on the achievements screen. This is likely Resource 173 instead.

entries.name: amount-value-killed-by-others
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the total military score gained by all other players from killing the current player's units. Probably isn't included in the actual military score calculations, otherwise some players would have negative military scores.

entries.name: amount-value-razed-by-others
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the total military score gained by all other players from razing the current player's buildings. Probably isn't included in the actual military score calculations, otherwise some players would have negative military scores.

entries.name: amount-killed-by-others
entries.description: The total number of the player's units killed by the player's enemies. Likely is equal to Units Lost in the achievements screen.

entries.name: amount-razed-by-others
entries.description: The total number of the player's buildings by the player's enemies. Likely is equal to Buildings Lost in the achievements screen.

entries.name: amount-value-current-units
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the economy score gained from the player's current units.

entries.name: amount-value-current-buildings
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the economy score gained from the player's current buildings.

entries.name: amount-food-total
entries.description: The total amount of food gathered, including food from feitorias and food bought at the market. Food from tribute is not included. Food sold at the market is not subtracted from this total.

entries.name: amount-wood-total
entries.description: The total amount of wood gathered, including wood from feitorias and wood bought at the market. Wood from tribute is not included. Wood sold at the market is not subtracted from this total.

entries.name: amount-stone-total
entries.description: The total amount of stone gathered, including stone from feitorias and stone bought at the market. Stone from tribute is not included. Gold lost from buying resources at the market is not subtracted from this total.

entries.name: amount-gold-total
entries.description: The total amount of gold gathered, including gold from trade carts, trade cogs, relics, feitorias, and gold from selling resources at the market. Stone sold at the market is not subtracted from this total.

entries.name: amount-total-value-of-kills
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the military score gained from killing enemy units.

entries.name: amount-total-tribute-received
entries.description: The total amount of tribute received.

entries.name: amount-total-value-of-razings
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the military score gained from razing enemy buildings.

entries.name: amount-total-castles-built
entries.description: The total number of castles the player built. Likely equal to Total Castles in the achievements screen.

entries.name: amount-total-wonders-built
entries.description: The total number of wonders the player built. Likely equal to Total Wonders in the achievements screen.

entries.name: amount-tribute-score
entries.description: Likely either the score the player gained from sending tribute or the total resources tributed + tribute taxes.

entries.name: amount-convert-min-adj
entries.description: An adjustment to the minimum amount of time a monastery unit must spend converting before a unit will be converted. Inquisition sets this to -1.

entries.name: amount-convert-max-adj
entries.description: An adjustment to the maximum amount of time a monastery unit must spend converting units. After this time, the unit will automatically be converted. Inquisition sets this to -1.

entries.name: amount-convert-resist-min-adj
entries.description: An adjustment to the conversion resistance of units. Likely adjusts the minimum amount of time monastery units must spend converting these units before they will be converted. Used by Faith, Devotion, and the Teutons team bonus.

entries.name: amount-convert-resist-max-adj
entries.description: An adjustment to the conversion resistance of units. Likely adjusts the maximum amount of time monastery units must spend converting these units. After this time, the unit will automatically be converted. Used by Faith, Devotion, and the Teutons team bonus.

entries.name: amount-convert-building-min
entries.description: An adjustment to the minimum amount of time a monastery unit must spend converting before a building will be converted. Inquisition sets this to -5.

entries.name: amount-convert-building-max
entries.description: An adjustment to the maximum amount of time a monastery unit must spend converting buildings. After this time, the building will automatically be converted. Inquisition sets this to -5.

entries.name: amount-convert-building-chance
entries.description: The percent chance a monastery unit will successfully convert a unit each second within the minimum and maximum conversion times for the object. Default is 25%. Inquisition increases this resource to 5.

entries.name: amount-spies
entries.description: Likely set to 1 if Spies is researched.

entries.name: amount-value-wonders-castles
entries.description: Likely either the total cost or the amount of society score gained from constructing castles and wonders.

entries.name: amount-food-score
entries.description: Likely the amount of economic score gained from the player's current food stockpile.

entries.name: amount-wood-score
entries.description: Likely the amount of economic score gained from the player's current wood stockpile.

entries.name: amount-stone-score
entries.description: Likely the amount of economic score gained from the player's current stone stockpile.

entries.name: amount-gold-score
entries.description: Likely the amount of economic score gained from the player's current gold stockpile.

entries.name: amount-wood-bonus
entries.description: The Mayan bonus for wood, where wood resources last longer.

entries.name: amount-food-bonus
entries.description: The Mayan bonus for food, where food resources last longer.

entries.name: amount-relic-rate
entries.description: The rate that relics accumulate gold. Default is 30. Changed by Sultans and Aztec team bonus.

entries.name: amount-heresy
entries.description: Set to 1 when the player researches Heresy.

entries.name: amount-theocracy
entries.description: Set to 1 when the player researches Theocracy.

entries.name: amount-crenellations
entries.description: Set to 1 when the player researches Crenellations. Probably controls whether garrisoned infantry fire arrows.

entries.name: amount-construction-rate-mod
entries.description: Modifies the construction rate of buildings. Used by the Spanish.

entries.name: amount-hun-wonder-bonus
entries.description: Affects the victory time of wonders. Probably also affects relic victory times. Seems to be the number of years required for victory * 10. Used for Atheism.

entries.name: amount-spies-discount
entries.description: Atheism sets this to 1. Likely applies the 50% discount to Spies if this resource is set to 1.

entries.name: amount-feitoria-food-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of food obtained from owning n number of Feitorias is given by n * amount-feitoria-food-productivity * 1.6.

entries.name: amount-feitoria-wood-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of wood obtained from owning n number of Feitorias is given by n * amount-feitoria-wood-productivity * 0.7.

entries.name: amount-feitoria-stone-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of stone obtained from owning n number of Feitorias is given by n * amount-feitoria-stone-productivity * 0.3.

entries.name: amount-feitoria-gold-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of gold obtained from owning n number of Feitorias is given by n * amount-feitoria-gold-productivity * 1.0.

entries.name: amount-temporary-map-reveal
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. If > 0, enemy TCs are revealed. Set to 5 for Vietnamese.

entries.name: amount-reveal-initial-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Reveals relics on the map for Burmese.

entries.name: amount-elevation-bonus-higher
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The fraction for additional bonus damage dealt from higher elevation. 0.25 for Tatars. Damage that units on higher elevation deal to units on lower elevation is multiplied by 1.25 + amount-elevation-bonus-higher.

entries.name: amount-elevation-bonus-lower
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The fraction for additional bonus damage dealt from lower elevation. Not used for Tatars. Damage that units on lower elevation deal to units on higher elevation is multiplied by 0.75 + amount-elevation-bonus-lower.

entries.name: amount-raiding-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Used for keshik gold generation per 100 seconds. Set to 50 for Tatars.

entries.name: amount-mercenary-kipchak-count
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The total number of mercenary kipchaks creatable. Researching Cuman Mercenaries sets this to 5 * the number of amount-castle.

entries.name: amount-mercenary-kipchak-limit
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The total number of trained and/or queued mercenary kipchaks.

entries.name: amount-shepherd-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The Tatars bonus for sheep lasting longer.

entries.name: amount-shared-line-of-sight
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. No longer used.

entries.name: amount-feudal-town-center-limit
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. This is the number of extra TCs a player is allowed to build IF TCs are enabled in feudal age. Default is 1. Cumans sets this to 2.

entries.name: amount-fishing-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Mayan bonus for fishing lasting longer.

entries.name: amount-unused-0
entries.description: Unused. Might be usable by mods.

entries.name: amount-monument-food-trickle
entries.description: Defined as "amount-unused-1". The monument food trickle modifier. The amount of resources obtained by owning a monument is 0.7925 * amount-monument-food-trickle.

entries.name: amount-monument-wood-trickle
entries.description: Defined as "amount-unused-2". The monument wood trickle modifier. The amount of resources obtained by owning a monument is 0.7925 * amount-monument-wood-trickle.

entries.name: amount-monument-stone-trickle
entries.description: Defined as "amount-unused-3". The monument stone trickle modifier. The amount of resources obtained by owning a monument is 0.7925 * amount-monument-stone-trickle.

entries.name: amount-monument-gold-trickle
entries.description: Defined as "amount-unused-4". The monument gold trickle modifier. The amount of resources obtained by owning a monument is 0.7925 * amount-monument-gold-trickle.

entries.name: amount-relic-food-rate
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Amount of food generated per minute per relic captured. Set to 30 for Burgundians. Affected by Atheism.

entries.name: amount-villagers-killed-by-gaia
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Total number of villagers lost to gaia.

entries.name: amount-villagers-killed-by-animal
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Total number of villagers lost to wild animals.

entries.name: amount-villagers-killed-by-ai-player
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Total number of villagers lost to AIs.

entries.name: amount-villagers-killed-by-human-player
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Total number of villagers lost to human players.

entries.name: amount-food-generation
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Free food trickle rate per minute. Used in Battle Royale.

entries.name: amount-wood-generation
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Free wood trickle rate per minute. Used in Battle Royale.

entries.name: amount-stone-generation
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Free stone trickle rate per minute. USed in Battle Royale.

entries.name: amount-gold-generation
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Free gold trickle rate per minute. Used in Battle Royale.

entries.name: amount-spawn-cap
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Sets the limit to the number of buildings that can spawn objects for civ bonuses. Probably affected by Nomad.

entries.name: amount-flemish-militia-pop
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Number of alive flemish militia.

entries.name: amount-gold-farming-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Farming gold production rate per 100 seconds. Burgundian Vinegards tech sets this to 2.

entries.name: amount-folwark-collection-amount
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of food immediately collected from farms around a folwark. Affected by mill technologies and civ bonuses.

entries.name: amount-folwark-collection-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The ID of the resource (0 = food, 1 = wood, 2 = stone, 3 = gold) that is given when a farm is constructed around a folwark. Set to 0 for Poles.

entries.name: amount-building-id
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The ID of the building that the folwark needs to upgrade from for the farm collection ability to work. Set to 68 (mill) for Poles.

entries.name: amount-units-converted
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of units lost to enemy conversions.

entries.name: amount-stone-gold-mining-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Gold production rate while mining stone per 100 seconds. Set to 18 for Poles and is modified by stone gathering techs.

entries.name: amount-workshop-food-trickle
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Trade workshop food production rate multiplier. The amount of food obtained from owning n number of trade workshops (Unit 1647) is given by n * amount-workshop-food-trickle * 2.25.

entries.name: amount-workshop-wood-trickle
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Trade workshop wood production rate multiplier. The amount of wood obtained from owning n number of trade workshops (Unit 1647) is given by n * amount-workshop-wood-trickle * 2.25.

entries.name: amount-workshop-stone-trickle
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Trade workshop stone production rate multiplier. The amount of stone obtained from owning n number of trade workshops (Unit 1647) is given by n * amount-workshop-stone-trickle * 2.25.

entries.name: amount-workshop-gold-trickle
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Trade workshop gold production rate multiplier. The amount of gold obtained from owning n number of trade workshops (Unit 1647) is given by n * amount-workshop-gold-trickle * 2.25.

entries.name: amount-units-value-total
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The total cost of all units trained so far. This does not decrease when units are killed.

entries.name: amount-buildings-value-total
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The total cost of all buildings constructed so far. This does not decrease when buildings are destroyed.

entries.name: amount-villagers-created-total
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The total number of all villagers trained so far. This does not decrease when villagers are killed.

entries.name: amount-villagers-idle-periods-total
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The number of villagers that entered an idle state since the game started. This is only updated every 5 physical minutes, and the starting villagers are added to this resource at the beginning of the game since they start out idle.

entries.name: amount-villagers-idle-seconds-total
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The amount of total seconds all villagers have been idle since the start of the game. This is only updated every 5 physical minutes. Any villagers immediately add their idle time to this resource if they die.

entries.name: amount-trade-food-percent
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The percentage of gold generated from trade that is also given as food. Bengalis sets this to 10.

entries.name: amount-trade-wood-percent
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The percentage of gold generated from trade that is also given as wood.

entries.name: amount-trade-stone-percent
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The percentage of stone generated from trade that is also given as food.

entries.name: amount-livestock-food-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Garrisoned herdable food generation rate per 60 seconds. Gurjaras sets this to 3.5.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-building-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The ID of the building to use for the speed up effect. This is set to the caravanserai by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-building-range
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. This specifies the range (in tiles) of the square area created around the speed up building for the speed up effect. The speed up building is specified by amount-speed-up-building-type. Set to 8 by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-percentage
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The adjustment used when a unit matching the amount-speed-up-object-type is within the amount-speed-up-building-range of the speed up building. Set to 0.2 (20%) by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-object-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The class ID (900+) of units that should be affected by the speed up effect. Set to 919 (trade-cart-class) by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-effect-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The type of effect caused by the speed up building. Possible values are 5 (movement speed), 13 (work rate), and 109 (regeneration). Set to 5 by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-secondary-effect-type
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. This is the type of secondary effect caused by the speed up building. Uses same values as amount-speed-up-effect-type. Set to 109 (regeneration) by default.

entries.name: amount-speed-up-secondary-percentage
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The adjustment used for the secondary speed up effect type when a unit matching the amount-speed-up-object-type is within the amount-speed-up-building-range of the speed up building. Set to 60 by default (60 HP per minute).

entries.name: amount-civ-name-override
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Unknown.

entries.name: amount-starting-scout-id
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The unit ID of the starting scout.

entries.name: amount-relic-wood-rate
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The relic wood production per minute.

entries.name: amount-relic-stone-rate
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The relic stone production per minute.

entries.name: amount-chopping-gold-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Gold production while lumberjacks chop wood per 100 seconds. Affected by Paper Money.

entries.name: amount-foraging-wood-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Wood production while foragers gather food per 100 seconds. Set to 10.4753 for Portuguese.

entries.name: amount-hunting-productivity
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Gold production while hunters gather food per 100 seconds.

entries.name: amount-technology-reward-effect
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The ID of an additional effect which will fire when any technology is researched.

entries.name: amount-unit-repair-cost
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The percentage of cost required to repair siege units and ships. Set to 0.5 by default.

entries.name: amount-building-repair-cost
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. The percentage of cost required to repair buildings. Set to 0.5 by default. Affected by Georgians team bonus.

entries.name: amount-elevation-damage-higher
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Damage modifier for own units when attacked from higher elevation.

entries.name: amount-elevation-damage-lower
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Damage modifier for own units when attacked from lower elevation. Georgians modifies this by -0.15.

entries.name: amount-infantry-kill-reward
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. This resource currently effectively enables/disables gold generation per second by infantry killing villagers, trade units and monks. Affected by Chieftains.

entries.name: amount-military-can-convert
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Military units with the conversion task can convert units if this is set to > 0 for a player.

entries.name: amount-military-conversion-range-adj
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Adds to the conversion range of military units. Probably only affects military units that can convert, not monks. Set to 6 by default.

entries.name: amount-military-conversion-chance
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Determines the conversion probability per monk second. Probably only affects military units that can convert, not monks. Set to 25 by default.

entries.name: amount-military-conversion-recharge-rate
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Determines the faith recharge rate after successful conversions. Probably only affects military units that can convert, not monks. Set to 1.6 by default.

entries.name: amount-spawn-stay-inside
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. Used to spawn one relic in one Armenian fortified church once constructed.

entries.name: amount-cavalry-kill-reward
entries.description: DE only. Must be defined with a defconst. This resource effectively sets the gold generation rate per second by cavalry fighting other military units. Used to be used by Persians.

families.description: The scouting method.

entries.name: scout-center
entries.description: Scout around the center of the map.

entries.name: scout-opposite
entries.description: Scouts the point on the opposite side of the map from position-self. It is found reflecting position-self across the center of the map.

entries.name: scout-corner
entries.description: Scouts the location of the corner closest to position-self (the location of the player's oldest Town Center).

entries.name: scout-enemy
entries.description: This parameter will send the scout back to the target enemy's nearest building +/- 8 tiles in any direction at random, in order to better explore the target's town. If your ally finds the enemy town, you can target it for attacks, but not for forward building, since placement rejects the black area. With scout-enemy, you can discover the terrain near the building found by your ally.

entries.name: scout-border
entries.description: Scouts the point on a border that is closest to position-self (the location of the player's oldest Town Center).

entries.name: scout-mirror
entries.description: Scouts the expected position of the mirrored opponent on the opposite team, found by mirroring from position-self across the line that separates teams.

entries.name: scout-flank
entries.description: Scouts the expected position where the nearest enemy flank player should be, found by evaluating all of the scout-opposite points for all members of the team and picking the closest point.
